http_semantics.note: The request-side-decidable error (delete_vectors naming a vector that does not exist in a collection whose only vector is the unnamed default) was surfaced as HTTP 400 with a descriptive body — not 2xx-masked. The defect is temporal: the 400 is a MID-EXECUTION rejection emitted after the prefix operations of the same request had already been applied and durably committed (wait=true), so the client is told the request failed while server state changed.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: batch operations are applied sequentially in the order given; each operation reports its own result
contract_grounding.note: Violates-declaration self-check: the claim's phenomenon is 'rejected request committed state', not 'illegal value silently accepted' — the request WAS rejected (400), so this is the Type4 state-consistency face, and violates=true means the constraint's composite promise broke on the rejection path: ops 1-2 were applied sequentially (order clause honored) but reported no result of their own (no per-op results in a 400 envelope — the accumulated results vector is discarded), and a whole-request rejection coexists with durably committed prefix state (612 visible with the full CTL-style payload). The doc prose behind the constraint contains the 'executed in order' wording verbatim but is silent on rollback/atomicity (recorded as content_consistency PARTIAL); the violated rejection-semantics reading is the framework's state-consistency principle (a rejected request must leave no state change), which the doc neither promises nor contradicts. The observed parameter (operations array of UpdateOperation) is squarely inside the quote's constraint domain, so no constraint re-citation is needed.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST POST /collections/{name}/points/batch → update_batch (src/actix/api/update_api.rs:328) → do_batch_update_points (src/common/update.rs:752) → sequential for-loop applying each op via do_upsert_points / do_set_payload / do_delete_vectors etc., EVERY arm using `.await?` → per-op toc update → shard WAL append + apply (durable at wait=true) → segment-layer vector-name validation fires only at APPLY time of that op (OperationError::VectorNameNotExists, defined lib/segment/src/common/operation_error.rs:27) → From<OperationError> for CollectionError::BadInput (lib/collection/src/operations/types.rs:1110) → StorageError::WrongInput 'Wrong input: ...' → actix HTTP 400. On the first failing op the whole function early-returns Err: (a) NO whole-batch pre-validation of operations before any application (the only up-front loop is the strict-mode check), (b) NO rollback or compensation of already-applied prefix ops, (c) NO partial-results reporting (results vec discarded). This exactly produces the observed position-dependent behavior: poison last → prefix committed + 400 (F leg); poison first → nothing applied + 400 (G leg).
